newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pierre Fabre withdraws anti-lice spray in France.
newsitem.headline: Pierre Fabre withdraws anti-lice spray in France.

text.p: French pharmaceutical company Pierre Fabre said on Monday it had withdrawn its Itax anti-lice aerosol spray from the market.
The move follows a restriction on all anti-lice aerosols by the French drug regulator L'Agence du Medicament, which last week banned their use by asthmatic children, a company spokeswoman said.
The company sold 6,090 of the sprays in 1996 for around 49 francs each, she said.
She was confirming an article in Monday's issue of financial daily Les Echos, which said that SmithKline Beecham's French unit had also withdrawn its anti-lice aerosol spray Marie Rose.

An official at the French subsidiary of Anglo-American drugs firm SmithKline Beecham said its product had been withdrawn anyway since end-February for commercial reasons, but it had now withdrawn stocks which remained in pharmacies and would not reintroduce the product.
Drug regulators last Monday said pharmaceutical firms must now mark on anti-lice aerosols that these must not be used by asthmatics.
Other brands are being withdrawn but will be reintroduced with the new warning, the SmithKline official said.

A spokeswoman at the regulator said there were many brands of such aerosols on sale in France. Some were authorised drugs, others were not authorised and were sold in parapharmacies, or non-medical chemists' shops, she said.
She declined to give the names of other brands.
The change comes after a child who suffered from asthma died after using an anti-lice aerosol spray, the regulator said.
Anti-lice shampoos and lotions do not represent a danger for asthmatics, it said.
